item.title: LightlySSL Adds World Model Training with LeWM for Image-based Agents
item.description:
LightlySSL Adds World Model Training with LeWM for Image-based Agents

LightlySSL, a Python library and computer vision framework for self-supervised learning and latent world models on images, has introduced new world model training capabilities. The update allows the system to learn how a scene responds to actions using the LeWM architecture, enabling planning in its own embedding space.

🧩 How it works

The new LeWM component learns from raw frames and actions without requiring rewards, labels, or a map of the environment. It trains through random play. Once trained, the model plans by imagining the outcome of each move within its embedding space. This allows agents to find paths to goals, such as navigating through a door to a target location, based solely on a picture of that goal.

⚙️ Key details

LightlySSL is built with a modular framework that exposes low-level building blocks, including loss functions and model heads. It is written in a PyTorch-like style and supports custom backbone models for self-supervised pre-training. The framework also supports distributed training using PyTorch Lightning.

Users can access the functionality by installing the library with PyTorch version 2.0 or later.

Component Description
LeWM Learns scene responses to actions from raw frames and plans via imagined outcomes
LeJEPA Self-supervised learning support added in May 2026
LightlyStudio Open-source project for visualizing, annotating, and managing data
LightlyTrain New project making SSL and distillation pretraining accessible in a few lines of code

🚀 Availability

The library is available for installation via pip. A commercial version is offered with additional features, including Docker support and pretraining models for embedding, classification, detection, and segmentation tasks. This commercial version also includes a platform with active learning and data curation features.

#LightlySSL #SelfSupervisedLearning #WorldModels #ComputerVision #LeWM

item.title: New World Model Research Papers Expand Capabilities in Robotics and Autonomous Systems
item.description:
New World Model Research Papers Expand Capabilities in Robotics and Autonomous Systems

Researchers have released multiple new papers advancing world models for robotics, autonomous driving, and video generation. These developments focus on creating more robust and versatile models that can handle complex real-world scenarios through semantic understanding, temporal reasoning, and closed-loop simulation capabilities.

📚 New Papers Introduced

Multiple research groups have published papers on advanced world models across different applications:

  • ST-WAM: Semantic-Temporal World Action Model for Robust Manipulation under Visual Distribution Shifts
  • NVIDIA OmniDreams: Real-Time Generative World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous Vehicle Simulation
  • Cosmos 3: Omnimodal World Models for Physical AI
  • X Square Robot WALL-WM: Carving World Action Modeling at the Event Joints
  • GE-Sim 2.0: A Roadmap Towards Comprehensive Closed-loop Video World Simulators for Robotic Manipulation
  • Xiaomi EV World Model: A Joint World Model Integrating Reconstruction and Generation for Autonomous Driving
  • Coowa: The DAWN of World-Action Interactive Models
  • Being-H0.7: A Latent World-Action Model from Egocentric Videos
  • MotuBrain: An Advanced World Action Model for Robot Control
  • Cortex 2.0: Grounding World Models in Real-World Industrial Deployment
  • HY-World 2.0: A Multi-Modal World Model for Reconstructing, Generating, and Simulating 3D World
  • Helios: Real Real-Time Long Video Generation Model
  • Seedance 2.0: Advancing Video Generation for World Complexity
  • Matrix-Game 3.0: Real-Time and Streaming Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
  • HY-Embodied-0.5: Embodied Foundation Models for Real-World Agents
  • OpenWorldLib: A Unified Codebase and Definition of Advanced World Models
  • ABot-PhysWorld: Interactive World Foundation Model for Robotic Manipulation with Physics Alignment
  • GigaWorld-Policy: An Efficient Action-Centered World–Action Model
  • GigaBrain-0.5M*: a VLA That Learns From World Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

🔍 Paper Details

Model Name Application Focus Additional Notes
ST-WAM Robotic manipulation Handles visual distribution shifts
NVIDIA OmniDreams Autonomous vehicles Closed-loop simulation
Cosmos 3 Physical AI Omnimodal approach
WALL-WM Robot control at event joints Novel modeling approach
GE-Sim 2.0 Robotic manipulation Comprehensive closed-loop simulators
Xiaomi EV World Model Autonomous driving Joint reconstruction and generation

🚀 Availability

All papers include associated resources:

  • Papers are available on arXiv
  • Several projects provide code repositories:
    • ST-WAM: https://github.com/Thu-WangMX/ST-WAM-Semantic-Temporal-World-Action-Model
    • HY-World 2.0: https://github.com/Tencent-Hunyuan/HY-World-2.0
    • WALL-WM: https://github.com/X-Square-Robot/wall-x
    • OpenWorldLib: Available through repository
    • Helios: https://github.com/PKU-YuanGroup/Helios
  • Some projects provide website resources for additional information

💡 Research Context

These papers are part of an ongoing effort to advance world models for general video generation, embodied AI, and autonomous driving applications. Researchers invite contributions through pull requests and citations to this growing collection of world model research.

item.title: Solar framework launches open tools for real-time video world models
item.description:
Solar framework launches open tools for real-time video world models

Solar is an open framework for interactive world models that spans open data, scalable training, long-horizon video generation, and real-time deployment. The repository contains code for two primary components: SolarWM and SolarRenderer.

🧩 How it works

The framework is built around two distinct modules that handle different aspects of video generation and rendering:

Component Function
SolarWM Enables real-time interaction, continuous exploration, and diverse generated worlds.
SolarRenderer Performs four-step, structure-conditioned video rendering with bidirectional and block-causal training and inference on MiniMax-H3.

⚙️ Key details

Several specific model releases and optimizations are included in the Solar framework:

  • SolarWM-H3 Memory: Improves long-term scene consistency and preserves visual details across revisits. Weights are available for the 33B model.
  • SolarWM-H3 Realtime: Enables low-latency interactive video generation from an image and a prompt, featuring real-time camera control.
  • H3 Streaming VAE Decoder: Allows for low-latency streaming video decoding that produces frames as latents arrive. It supports both the official MiniMax-H3 VAE and NVIDIA’s distilled StreamRender-H3 decoder.
  • Training Efficiency: Training for SolarWM-H3 is speeded up by 1.9–2.1× across Stage0.5, Stage1, and Stage2 with matching training trajectories, attributed to ResearchBoost-Agent.
  • Data: The SolarWM dataset and SolarRenderer dataset are hosted on Hugging Face.

🚀 Availability

  • Code: SolarWM and SolarRenderer code is available in the repository. Real-time deployment for SolarWM and the H3 Streaming VAE Decoder code are located in the deploy/solar_wm/ directory.
  • Weights: Model weights for both SolarWM and SolarRenderer are available on Hugging Face.
  • Demonstrations: An online demo for SolarRenderer is available on Hugging Face Spaces.
  • Documentation: Specific documentation for SolarWM is found in docs/solar_wm/ and for SolarRenderer in docs/solar_renderer/.

#SolarFramework #VideoGeneration #WorldModels #OpenSource #MiniMax-H3

Source: Junchao-cs/SolarWM

item.title: Evaluating Latent Safety Filters and Conservatism in World Models
item.description:
Evaluating Latent Safety Filters and Conservatism in World Models

A new approach uses a latent safety filter based on a world model’s latent to decide whether a planned action is safe, utilizing conformal calibration to set thresholds.

🧩 How it works

  • A latent safety filter decides from the latent of a world model whether a planned action is safe.
  • Conformal calibration sets the threshold of the filter so that it accepts an unsafe action only with a small probability.
  • To measure conservatism, similar latents and actions are grouped into cells.
  • A filter giving one decision per cell must refuse safe transitions in order to refuse unsafe ones within that cell, with this share of safe transitions called the overlap.
  • Both the overlap and conformal calibration can be applied to any latent.

⚙️ Key details

  • It is proven that the overlap is the minimum share of safe transitions that such a filter has to refuse in order to accept no unsafe transition in the data.
  • The overlap and conformal calibration were used to compare three existing designs where safety labels train:
    • A classifier on top of the world model
    • The world model itself
    • A separate encoder beside it
Design Variant Performance in Visual Navigation
Separate encoder beside the world model Lowest overlap, refuses the fewest safe actions at the same conformal level, and lets the planner reach the most goals among the three

#ArtificialIntelligence #MachineLearning #WorldModels #SafetyFilters

Source: Measuring the Conservatism of Latent Safety Filters for World Models

item.title: Google rolls out updated Project Genie with Genie 4 agent and community gallery
item.description:
Google rolls out updated Project Genie with Genie 4 agent and community gallery

Google has rolled out a new Project Genie experience to eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers, introducing Genie 4, upgrades to Genie 3, a Project Genie agent, and a community gallery for discovering and remixing interactive worlds.

🔍 Overview

  • Project Genie combines advanced world models with Gemini models to generate, explore, and shape interactive worlds directly from a browser.
  • The update makes worlds more responsive, creative, and social based on early tester feedback.

🧩 Key Features

Genie 4

  • Most realistic and interactive world model yet.
  • Allows prompting mid-session to change the world in real time (e.g., shift weather, add characters, redirect action).
  • Includes real-time native audio that adapts to the scene, from ambient soundscapes to character dialogue.
  • Delivers highest-fidelity visuals, physics, and native audio.

Genie 3 Updates

  • Exploration extended to up to 3 minutes per generation (previously 60 seconds).
  • Ability to link multiple worlds for longer journeys.
  • Seed new worlds from 360-degree panorama images.
  • Dynamically change the environment with natural-language prompts during exploration.
  • Remains available in the model picker for longer runs or panorama-seeded spaces.

Project Genie Agent

  • Enables creation through natural-language conversation.
  • Orchestrates Google’s multimodal models to craft initial visuals and custom background scores.
  • Allows bringing Gemini models into sessions for context-aware suggestions and automatic in-world event triggers.

Community Gallery

  • Curated worlds and community creations available for exploration and remixing.
  • Highlights include “Living Memory” (personal photos transformed into explorable spaces), “Dino Field Guide” (prehistoric habitats from 360-degree panoramas), and “Rock Paper Scissors” (themed objects with Gemini as real-time referee).
  • Collaborations with creators: “Villa Giallo” (gothic manor mystery with Will aka BLVCKL!GHT) and “The Life of Ants” (ant colony navigation with filmmaker Anand Gandhi).
  • Users can publish their own creations for others to explore and remix.

⚙️ Model Comparison

Model Key Capabilities
Genie 4 Highest-fidelity visuals, physics, native audio; real-time mid-session prompting; real-time adaptive audio
Genie 3 Up to 3-minute generations; link multiple worlds; panorama seeding; mid-session natural-language environment changes

🚀 Availability

  • Eligible Google AI Ultra subscribers can access the new Project Genie experience starting today.
  • Google AI Pro members can join the waitlist on the same page.

💡 Responsible Development

  • All generated video and audio includes SynthID watermarking.
  • All model inputs and outputs undergo safety screenings.
  • Genie 3 and Genie 4 remain frontier research models; active challenges include camera latency, intricate physical interactions, real-time audio precision, and long-term scene permanence.
  • A Genie 4 model research overview provides deeper details on limitations and progress.

#Google #AI #WorldModels #GenerativeAI #InteractiveWorlds #Genie

Source: Genie 4 is now available

item.title: Microsoft Research Introduces Quine Multimodal World Model for Biology
item.description:
Microsoft Research Introduces Quine Multimodal World Model for Biology

Microsoft Research has introduced Quine, a research effort to create a multimodal world model of biology and an interactive harness that connects models, scientific tools, literature, and researchers.

🔍 Overview

Quine is designed to work across various biological boundaries, reflecting a vision for a discovery system that evolves through scientific use. It consists of two primary components:

  • A world model of biology: A system capable of representing the state of a biological system, predicting how that state evolves in response to interventions, and reasoning over the consequences of those interventions multiple steps into the future.
  • An interactive harness: A system that connects the world model to orchestration and reasoning models, scientific tools, literature, and research teams.

🧩 How it works

The core world model learns shared representations across biological modalities and scales, including:

  • Sequence
  • Structure
  • Function
  • Cellular state
  • Imaging data

By training across these modalities jointly, Quine can use evidence from one modality to inform predictions in another, capturing relationships that might be lost when separate single-domain specialist models are used. This integration allows researchers to generate predictions across modalities and reason about the consequences of biological interventions before wet-lab testing.

⚙️ Key details

Microsoft Research has applied Quine in collaboration with researchers at the Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard to study pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Through this work, they have used the system to prioritize compounds predicted to drive therapeutic tumor-state shifts and validated several top-ranked candidates across multiple wet-lab assays.

Quine is experimental research technology intended only for research, not for clinical or medical use. Its outputs may be incomplete or inaccurate and require review by qualified researchers and appropriate scientific and experimental validation.

🚀 Availability

  • Quine Fellows program: A cohort of scientists will be given access to the system to accelerate their research and provide scientific feedback.
  • Future Access: As the technology matures, Microsoft expects to expand access through products such as Microsoft Discovery.

#MicrosoftResearch #Biology #WorldModels #Biotech #AI

Source: Introducing Quine: An AI research system designed for the complexity of biology

item.title: Foundation Models and Learned World Models Reshaping the Game Lifecycle
item.description:
Foundation Models and Learned World Models Reshaping the Game Lifecycle

Foundation models and advances in learned game-world models are reshaping AI across the entire game lifecycle, moving beyond simply playing games to supporting design, development, and runtime adaptation.

🔍 Overview

Recent systems now model players and game dynamics, support development and design, adapt player-facing experiences at runtime, and evaluate resulting artifacts. This literature is organized into six specific roles based on the immediate use of the AI output:

AI Role Primary Function
Playing and acting Executing actions within the game
Modeling players and games Simulating player behavior and game dynamics
Designing games Supporting the game design process
Building and maintaining games Assisting in development and maintenance
Generating and adapting at runtime Modifying experiences during active play
Testing and evaluating games Assessing game artifacts

🧩 How it works

There are identified cross-role connections where outputs from one role inform another:

  • Trajectories are used to train world models.
  • Learned environments provide experience for agents.
  • Design specifications drive executable implementations.
  • Feedback from play or testing guides revision.

⚙️ Key details

While capabilities can transfer across roles, certain elements often remain setting-specific, including:

  • Control schemes and rules
  • Engine interfaces
  • State representations
  • Player contexts

💡 Why it matters

The central challenge in this field is the ability to reuse or transfer outputs and capabilities across different roles while re-establishing evidence for effectiveness in specific game contexts. Currently, evaluation is most standardized for selected learned environments and bounded game playing. Other areas that remain less established include:

  • Persistent state in learned worlds
  • Repeated software revision
  • Validated player modeling
  • Sustained runtime adaptation
  • Representative automated testing

#FoundationModels #GameDevelopment #WorldModels #AI

Source: AI for Games in the Foundation Model Era

item.title: Former Google DeepMind Researcher Launches Stealth Startup for Humanoid Robot Training
item.description:
Former Google DeepMind Researcher Launches Stealth Startup for Humanoid Robot Training

Former Google DeepMind researcher Danijar Hafner has launched a new startup in San Francisco’s SoMa district to build AI that enables humanoid robots to navigate unfamiliar environments. Currently operating in stealth mode, the venture aims to solve the challenge of deploying robots in human spaces by training them using simulated physical realities.

🔍 Overview

Hafner’s brand-new startup is currently housed in an office with no name on the door. The physical space contains humanoids of various shapes and sizes, which are imported from China and hang like marionettes from racks in the center of the office.

The primary objective of the venture is to continue Hafner’s longtime work in enabling AI to successfully navigate environments that were not encountered during its training. This capability is critical for deploying robots in everyday human settings, such as a home, where a robot must handle a floor plan and furniture layout it has never seen before.

🧩 How it works

To bypass the traditional, real-world trial-and-error training usually required in robotics, Hafner relies on model-based reinforcement learning:

  • World Models: Hafner develops AI models designed to emulate physical reality.
  • Simulated Training: Agents are trained within these world models, treating them as real-world simulations to learn how to act.
  • Direct Execution: This approach allows the agents and the physical robots they control to execute massively complicated tasks without requiring physical training trials.

⚙️ Key developments

Over several years, Hafner has honed and proved his approach by pitting agents trained within his world models against popular video games and physical reality.

Project or Agent Capabilities and Achievements
PlaNet A model that allowed agents to execute actions by planning ahead.
Dreamer 2 The first agent to achieve human-level performance playing Atari 2600 games using a world model.
Dreamer 3 The first agent to solve the Minecraft Diamond challenge, successfully mining in-game gems on its own.
Dreamer 4 Learned to mine diamonds from an offline dataset of recorded gameplay videos, without ever interacting with the game directly.
DayDreamer Used the Dreamer algorithm to let robots operate themselves in novel environments and react to new experiences (such as being pushed over) without any specific training.

💡 Background

The 31-year-old researcher has a long history of working with leading AI organizations:

  • Early Interest: Growing up in a rural town in northeastern Germany with classical musician parents, Hafner learned programming from a neighbor and took online AI courses during high school.
  • Academic and Research Roles: While studying engineering as a second-year undergraduate at the Hasso Plattner Institute in Potsdam in 2015, he secured a student researcher role at Google Brain.
  • Industry Experience: He went on to hold a dozen internships and positions at Google Brain and Google DeepMind across the UK, Canada, and the US.
  • Collaborations: During his career, he worked alongside industry legends including Geoffrey Hinton, who is often referred to as one of the godfathers of AI, and Ashish Vaswani, coauthor of the research paper “Attention Is All You Need.”
  • Industry Reception: Timothy Lillicrap, one of Hafner’s former managers and coauthors at Google, describes him as a “standout among standouts.”

Hafner left Google DeepMind in the fall of 2025 to launch this new startup, marking the physical embodiment and next evolution of his work.

#Robotics #DeepMind #WorldModels #AIagents

Source: This AI entrepreneur is developing agents that can plan ahead for the unexpected
